Hypothesis: We hypothesize that in liver tumors, overexpression of COL1A2 instigates pronounced ECM remodeling, which subsequently amplifies integrin-mediated FAK signaling. Rather than directly phosphorylating nuclear proteins, this signaling cascade facilitates the nuclear translocation of YAP/TAZ. In the nucleus, YAP/TAZ activate a transcriptional program that increases both the expression levels and the functional modifications (e.g., post-translational modifications) of key mRNA export components such as NXF1 and THO complex regulators. This orchestrated response selectively enhances the export of mRNAs encoding proteins that promote angiogenesis and metastasis, thereby driving tumor progression. To test this hypothesis, we will utilize state-of-the-art techniques including CRISPR interference for targeted gene modulation, spatial transcriptomics for high-resolution mapping of molecular changes within tumor microenvironments, and phosphoproteomics to capture dynamic protein modifications across the signaling cascade.
Abstract: In liver neoplasms, we propose that overexpression of COL1A2 triggers significant extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling, which in turn reinforces integrin-mediated FAK signaling. This enhanced mechanical signal promotes the nuclear translocation of transcriptional co-activators such as YAP/TAZ rather than directly phosphorylating nuclear proteins. Once in the nucleus, YAP/TAZ orchestrate a transcriptional program that upregulates and functionally modifies key mRNA export machinery components, including NXF1 and regulators of the THO complex. The net effect is a selective increase in the export of mRNAs encoding pro-angiogenic and pro-metastatic proteins, thereby accelerating liver tumor progression. Our approach will leverage advanced technologies—CRISPR interference to manipulate gene expression, spatial transcriptomics to map the spatial heterogeneity of signaling responses, and quantitative phosphoproteomics to monitor post-translational modifications—thus providing robust mechanistic insights and identifying novel therapeutic intervention points.
CausalChain: COL1A2 upregulation -> ECM remodeling -> Activation of integrin/FAK signaling -> Nuclear translocation of YAP/TAZ -> Upregulation and post-translational modification of mRNA export machinery (NXF1 and THO complex regulators) -> Selective export of pro-angiogenic/metastatic mRNAs -> Accelerated liver tumor progression
